FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_015  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 5 (correctness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` claims allocation “uses LIVE fingerprints” and “adapts to observed performance,” but `LoadBalancer` never consults `ModelSpec.fingerprint` anywhere in `_admissibility_mask`, `_redundancy_target`, `_objective`, `_check_feasibility`, `_balanced`, or `_solve_greedy`. The only inputs used are `L`, `c`, `tau`, `tasks`, and `role_map`. As a result, `update_fingerprints()` and `get_live_models()` have no effect on dispatch decisions; the advertised adaptive routing loop is functionally inert end-to-end.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_016  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 1 (logic)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` advances the FSM unconditionally with `round_complete=True` regardless of whether the round was actually complete, whether all allocated models responded, or whether recovery/retry/reallocation is still pending. This collapses the distinction between “responses received” and “round resolved,” making the progression logic inconsistent with the FSM contract and preventing the manager from pausing in-place for retry-based recoveries.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_017  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 5 (correctness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` only examines models present in the `responses` dict. If an allocated active model produces no entry at all (missing response, dropped dispatch, orchestration omission), no failure is detected, no timeout/empty handling occurs, no failure history is recorded, and no abort logic can trigger from that absence. This is a cross-area hole between allocation/dispatch assumptions and failure handling: silent non-response is treated as success-by-omission.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_018  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 1 (logic)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.75  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` accepts a `tasks` argument but never uses it for any invariant check, allocation reconciliation, failure completeness check, cost attribution, or reallocation policy. Consequently the manager cannot verify that the reported `responses` and `findings` correspond to the tasks supposedly dispatched in that round, so the orchestration layer has no end-to-end consistency check between planned work and observed outputs.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_019  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2 (interface)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `RoundResult` includes an `allocation` field, but `DynamicManager.process_round()` always stores `allocation=None` and the manager does not retain or thread the last allocation into round processing. This breaks the cross-area interface needed to tie failures, costs, missing responses, and task coverage back to what was actually assigned, undermining the management layer’s ability to reason about reallocation or dispatch correctness.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_020  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 1 (logic)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler` is initialized with the original model set and `DynamicManager.update_fingerprints()` iterates only over `self.failure_handler.active_models`, but `process_round()` updates fingerprints only if `not self.fsm.is_terminal`. Any terminal transition caused by convergence/diminishing/failure suppresses the final-round fingerprint update entirely, so the live metrics omit the most recent observed performance. That makes the adaptive history internally inconsistent across runs and invalidates any post-hoc analysis expecting complete per-round capability traces.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_021  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.kappa_adopt()` returns `1 - adoption_delta` with no validation or clamping. If `adoption_delta` falls outside [0,1]—which `add_round_findings()` permits—the combined convergence metric can become negative or exceed 1 before the final `min(...)`, distorting convergence semantics and allowing malformed external inputs to dominate stop decisions.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_022  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.65  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer.feasibility_probability()` accepts any positive `L_std` and directly computes a Gaussian tail probability using `model.L` as mean capacity, but there is no validation that `L >= 0`, `task_load >= 0`, or `L_std` is finite. NaN or infinite capacity parameters propagate into `math.erf` or probability comparisons, producing undefined dispatch behaviour in `dispatch_check()` without any explicit failure signal.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_023  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 4 (completeness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: The “real-time manager monitoring interface” is only partially integrated. `ManagerEventType` defines recovery events (`RETRY`, `REALLOCATE`, `EXCLUDE`, `ABORT`) and response/progress events (`MODEL_RESPONSE`, `ROUND_START`), but `DynamicManager`/`FailureHandler` never emit them when those actions or phases actually occur. The event stream therefore cannot serve as the advertised operational monitoring protocol; it reports some detections but not the manager decisions that follow from them.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_024  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 1 (logic)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` counts prior failures of the same type across the entire run (`same_type_count`) with no round scoping, cooldown, or reset after successful rounds. A model that fails twice early can be permanently escalated on a later isolated recurrence, even after long healthy operation. This makes escalation path-dependent in a way that is not tied to persistence or current reliability state.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_025  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.__init__()` does not reject duplicate `model_id` values. Multiple internal structures (`RoleAssignment.capability_scores`, `FailureHandler.models`, `_live_fingerprints`, `_round_metrics`, `_model_idx`, `role_map`) key by `model_id`, so duplicates silently overwrite earlier entries and create cross-component inconsistency between list-based model order and dict-based identity. This can corrupt assignment, accounting, and failure tracking without an immediate exception.

Definitive stance: there are additional missed findings, mainly in cross-area integration: the adaptive fingerprint loop is non-operative, round completion is asserted rather than validated, and the manager lacks the allocation/response/task reconciliation needed for correct orchestration.
